title: Options after the script
prompt: This program submits a small job. Some options come before the script and some after it. It prints the exit code, then the job's lines without their `app:` prefix. What does it print? Type each line on its own line.
program:
import os, subprocess

open("/tmp/args.py", "w").write("""
import sys
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate()
sc = spark.sparkContext
print("app:", sc.appName)
print("app:", sc.master)
print("app:", sys.argv[1:])
spark.stop()
""")

env = {**os.environ, "SPARK_LOCAL_IP": "127.0.0.1"}
run = subprocess.run(
    ["spark-submit", "--master", "local[1]", "--name", "error-digest",
     "/tmp/args.py", "--name", "nightly", "--master", "yarn", "2026-03-01"],
    capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
print(run.returncode)
for line in run.stdout.splitlines():
    if line.startswith("app:"):
        print(line[5:])
hints: `spark-submit` reads its own options up to the script's path. What does it do with the words after it?
Words after the script are handed to the script in `sys.argv`, even when they look like options. Spark never sees them.
So the name and the master come only from the options before `/tmp/args.py`. `yarn` is never used, so nothing is rejected.
explanation: `spark-submit` reads options until it reaches the script. Everything after `/tmp/args.py` is the script's business: `sys.argv[1:]` is `['--name', 'nightly', '--master', 'yarn', '2026-03-01']`, and Spark ignores those words. So the application is called `error-digest` and runs on `local[1]`, the values before the script, and the job finishes with exit code 0. `yarn` would have been rejected here (there's no Hadoop configuration), but it was never an option, only an argument. Put Spark's options first, always.
